author: human
request:
Feature request: visits can currently only be created, never corrected. Two
product decisions come with it, made here as the product owner:

- Non-goal NG-5 is narrowed: cancelling a booked visit stays out of scope,
  but correcting its date and description is now in. Record the narrowing
  the way the project records non-goal changes.
- The edit form is reachable by its URL alone: the owner detail page gains
  no edit link in this request. A visible entry point may come as a
  follow-up request.

Add editing for a booked visit:

- GET /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits/{visitId}/edit shows the visit
  form prefilled with that visit's current date and description. Reuse the
  existing visit form template (pets/createOrUpdateVisitForm) and its `visit`
  model attribute.
- POST to the same URL validates like visit creation (description required,
  date in the future). On success it updates that visit in place — the pet
  must not gain an additional visit record — and redirects to the owner
  detail page. On validation failure it redisplays the form.

Cover the new behavior with tests.

These are all the product decisions; no further product answer will come
during the work. Where a choice still seems open, take the narrowest reading
consistent with this request and record the open question rather than
waiting.

author: product-requirements-expert
title: Staff can correct a booked visit's date and description
summary: A booked visit's date and description can be corrected through a form reached by its address alone. The correction follows the booking rules, changes that visit in place without adding another, and returns to the owner's record.
acceptance_criteria: given a booked visit, when its correction form is opened, then the form shows that visit's current date and description
given a booked visit, when a description and a date later than today are submitted, then that visit is updated and the owner's record is shown
given a booked visit, when a correction is saved, then the pet has the same number of visits as before
given a blank description or a date of today or earlier, when the correction is submitted, then it is refused and the form is shown again naming the field
edge case 3: a correction naming a visit that does not exist, or that does not belong to the named pet, is refused and changes no visit
edge case 4: a visit whose date has passed cannot be saved as it stands; its correction must carry a date later than today
non_goals: cancelling a booked visit (NG-5, narrowed; see adr/2026-09-29-non-goal-visit-cancellation.md)
any link or button to the correction form on the owner's record or elsewhere (owner decision: reachable by URL alone; a visible entry point may come as a follow-up request)
moving a visit to another pet, or changing anything other than its date and description
notes: Owner-specified mechanism from intake line 1, for the design expert: GET and POST on /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits/{visitId}/edit; reuse template pets/createOrUpdateVisitForm and its `visit` model attribute; on success redirect to the owner detail page; on validation failure redisplay the form. Validation is the booking validation (description required, date later than today). Trap to watch: the existing @ModelAttribute("visit") loader creates a new Visit and adds it to the pet on every request, so an edit path that reuses it would add a visit instead of updating one. Decisions I took as reversible (narrowest reading): edge case 3 mirrors booking edge case 1, and how the refusal is presented is up to design; no success flash message is required; the form's New heading and Add Visit button label are not required to change; whether the correction form lists the pet's earlier visits is not a requirement either way. Open questions recorded in docs/prd.md: a link from the owner's record (owner named it as a possible follow-up), and whether past visits should be correctable (edge case 4 follows the request as stated). ADR index: docs/adr/README.md needs a row for adr/2026-09-29-non-goal-visit-cancellation.md; the README is outside my write scope. theVisitEditShouldRedisplayTheFormWhenValidationFails is data-driven over blank description, today, and a past date; theVisitEditShouldRefuseAVisitThatDoesNotBelongToThePet covers an unknown visit id and another pet's visit.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: Correction fits the owner aggregate and the existing VisitController seam (system-design § Contracts invariants, new 'Visit correction' paragraph). Visits are reached owner -> pet -> visit and written back through OwnerRepository, as booking does. There is no VisitRepository and none is added. Two adjustments make this minor rather than covered. (1) The @ModelAttribute("visit") loader gains an optional visitId path variable. On the edit routes it returns the pet's existing Visit, found through a new Pet lookup by identity, and never calls pet.addVisit. On the booking routes it keeps creating and attaching a new Visit. This defuses the trap the product expert flagged. (2) system-design gains the § Scale and Load section with its first row, the per-owner graph. Basis: grep and read of VisitController, Visit, Pet, Owner, the template, and VisitControllerTests (IDE oracle not connected; weaker basis). The template pets/createOrUpdateVisitForm is reused unchanged. Its form has no action attribute, so it posts back to the /edit URL. The visit['new'] heading and the Add Visit label are not required to change (prd-entry notes).
integration_points: Entry points: GET and POST /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits/{visitId}/edit in VisitController. They sit beside the /visits/new handlers and share the loader, the minVisitDate attribute, and the @InitBinder disallow list (id, *.id).

Binding target (POST edit): the existing persisted Visit that the loader resolved from the path, under the binder's existing allow-list shape. Only date and description are form fields; id and nested id stay disallowed. The target is never a Visit identified by any request field (security-principles § Realization, Mass assignment).

Target resolution: owners.findById(ownerId) -> owner.getPet(petId) -> pet visit lookup by visitId, re-resolved on every request (security-principles § Realization, Trusting cross-request state). An unknown visit id, or one held by another pet, throws IllegalArgumentException from the loader. This mirrors the booking refusal for a pet the owner does not hold (PRD Visits edge case 1 -> edge case 3). No save is reached. The message carries ids only (security-principles § Realization, Secret disclosure: the error page renders exception messages).
Success: owners.save(owner) merges the detached graph (open-in-view is off). The mutated Visit is updated in place. Then redirect:/owners/{ownerId}. No flash message is required.

Validation: @Valid on the bound Visit (@NotBlank description) plus the booking non-future-date check. That check is extracted into one private method that both POST handlers call, and it keeps field 'date' and code typeMismatch.visitDate. Any error redisplays pets/createOrUpdateVisitForm.

Double per boundary. Framework transport: MockMvc (@WebMvcTest(VisitController.class)), the sanctioned harness. Repository: the file's existing @MockitoBean OwnerRepository stub, extended with an owner whose pet holds a visit with a set id. This is a conscious exception under testing-principles § Mocking Policy: the WebMvc slice has no JPA, and a hand-written OwnerRepository would have to implement the whole JpaRepository surface. Assert the unchanged visit count on the stubbed owner's pet, and assert no save on refusal (then(owners).should(never()).save(any())).

patterns.description: loadPetWithVisit: the shared owner/pet resolution. It is extended with an optional visitId; the new-Visit creation stays on the booking path only.
Owner.getPet(Integer id): the by-identity lookup shape the new Pet visit lookup mirrors.
Insert-or-update over the same owner graph, saved through OwnerRepository; the precedent for correcting a child entity in place.

risks.risk: Reusing the loader unchanged would attach a blank new Visit to the pet on every edit request. Saving the owner would then persist it or fail validation, and the visit count would change.
risks.mitigation: The loader creates and attaches a new Visit only when no visitId is present. theVisitEditShouldNotAddAVisitToThePet pins this (system-design § Contracts, Visit correction paragraph).

risks.risk: Copying the date check into the new handler would add a second controller copy of a business rule, a fresh violation under architecture-principles § Pattern Catalog, Web controller.
risks.mitigation: One private check method serves both handlers (system-design § Contracts, Visit correction paragraph). Moving it to a Form validator stays with system-design Open Question 2.

risks.risk: Path: the correction loads one owner's full graph and scans the pets and one pet's visits (system-design § Scale and Load, one owner's graph row).
risks.mitigation: Simplest readable form: a linear stream or loop by identity. The row is unrecorded, treated as bounded.

risks.risk: Concurrent corrections to the same visit: the last merge wins, because no entity carries a version column.
risks.mitigation: Accepted at the demonstration baseline (security-principles § Realization, What this application is). There is no orphan removal on Pet.visits, so a concurrent booking is not deleted by a correction's merge.

notes: ADR index: added the docs/adr/README.md row for 2026-09-29-non-goal-visit-cancellation.md, as the product expert flagged, and updated the 2026-08-08 row's status to match its narrowed Status line. No new architectural ADR: the loader shape and the shared check are contained in this slice and recorded as current state. No design-doc-autofix records to audit. Open questions recorded rather than waited on (owner gave no further answer; narrowest reading taken). (a) A blank date binds to null and passes the date check on both booking and correction, because Visit.date has no @NotNull. The correction therefore mirrors booking. Whether a blank date must be refused is a product question for a follow-up, not REQ-VIS-003 scope. (b) The refusal for an unknown or foreign visit follows booking: an IllegalArgumentException rendered by the error page (a 500), not a 404. A distinct not-found presentation would be a cross-controller decision. (c) The system-design provenance banner still says every statement is derived. The designed statements added by slices since then make that banner increasingly inexact; banner wording is left to a doc-sync pass. (d) architecture-principles § Pattern Catalog still names the non-future-visit-date check as living in controller methods, which stays accurate. The brief needs no edit for this slice.

author: security-reviewer
approved_aspects: Mass assignment: the correction POST binds only the resolved Visit. Its bindable fields are date and description, since Visit.java declares only `private LocalDate date;` and `private String description;` beyond BaseEntity's id. The id stays blocked by the existing controller-wide binder at VisitController.java:55 `dataBinder.setDisallowedFields("id", "*.id");`, which the diff leaves intact. The Owner graph is taken with `@ModelAttribute(name = "owner", binding = false)`, so no request field reaches it.

IDOR and identifier tampering: the target visit is re-resolved on every request from path variables, going owner (findById), then owner.getPet(petId), then pet.getVisit(visitId). getVisit filters `!visit.isNew() && Objects.equals(visit.getId(), id)`, so a visit id belonging to another pet or owner is refused with IllegalArgumentException, the same way booking refuses a foreign pet. This meets the cross-request-state row of docs/security-principles.md.

Validation parity: processEditVisitForm carries `@Valid Visit visit` (NotBlank description) and calls the same extracted rejectNonFutureDate method as booking. No check was removed or weakened: the booking path's inline date check was moved into that shared method unchanged.

Error disclosure: the new exception message `"Visit with id " + visitId + " not found for pet with id " + pet.getId()` carries only integer identifiers from the path. It matches the neighbouring owner and pet messages and puts no secret on the error page that renders exception messages (docs/security-principles.md line 37).

XSS: no template is in the change set (`python3 scripts/changeset.py --name-only` lists only docs, Pet.java, VisitController.java and two test files). The visit description renders through escaped th:text at createOrUpdateVisitForm.html:53 ``. `grep -n -E 'utext|__\$'` on the visit form found no unescaped output and no preprocessing.

Persistence side effects: spring.jpa.open-in-view=false (application.properties:11), so a rejected correction that mutated the in-memory visit is never flushed. Only the success path calls owners.save(owner), through the repository with no hand-built query.

Exposed surface: the new GET and POST /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits/{visitId}/edit routes are documented in docs/system-design.md:82, and the threat table there covers them (lines 188 and 190). Missing auth and CSRF is the recorded demonstration baseline, not a finding.
Secrets: grepping added diff lines for password|secret|token|api_key|credential found no match.

Supply chain: build.gradle is unchanged and no dependencyCheckAnalyze plugin is configured (grep of build.gradle found none), so no NVD match ran in this review. `./gradlew dependencies` resolves Spring Boot 4.1.1, spring-webmvc 7.0.9, jackson-databind 3.1.5, Thymeleaf 3.1.5.RELEASE and hibernate-core 7.4.5.Final.
./gradlew test was not run in this review; the build-pass at line 7 records the gate.

author: test-reviewer

findings.location: src/test/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/owner/VisitControllerTests.java (correction tests); guards at VisitController.java processEditVisitForm `@ModelAttribute(name = "owner", binding = false)` and the class binder `dataBinder.setDisallowedFields("id", "*.id")` (VisitController.java:55)
findings.description: No test pins the identifier-tampering defence that system-design.md's threat table now claims for the correction route ("Visit correction takes its target only from the path"). The correction is the first route that binds a form onto an existing persisted Visit, so an `id` request parameter would rewrite the loaded visit's identity, and a body field could reach the owner graph, if either guard were removed. Removing `setDisallowedFields` or `binding = false` leaves all five declared tests green (grep -F -e setDisallowedFields -e binding src/test/java/.../VisitControllerTests.java finds nothing). A test would fail on that change, so this is a missing test, not a wish.
findings.fix: Add one test, e.g. theVisitEditShouldIgnoreAnIdentifierSubmittedWithTheCorrection: post a valid correction to BOOKED_VISIT_ID with an extra `id` param equal to OTHER_PETS_VISIT_ID (named constant), then assert bookedVisit.getId() is still BOOKED_VISIT_ID and the pet still holds exactly bookedVisit. Optionally add an `owner`-side field (e.g. `owner.firstName`) and assert the owner is unchanged, in the same or a second test.

recommendations: Row 3 of refusedCorrections (BOOKED_DESCRIPTION, PASSED_VISIT_DATE, DATE_FIELD) runs the same decision path as row 2 (date not after today). It exists to state PRD edge case 4, so it is defensible, but say so through the row's role rather than adding more rows.

theVisitEditShouldRefuseAVisitThatDoesNotBelongToThePet asserts only that some IllegalArgumentException is the root cause and that `save` never ran. Adding an assertion that OTHER_PETS_VISIT_ID's visit keeps its date and description would state the 'changes no visit' half of edge case 3 directly. Not verified in this review whether a message assertion would be stable across the loader's other IllegalArgumentException paths.

The `extracting(Visit::getDate, Visit::getDescription)` chain is acceptable because Visit defines no equals (grep -F -e equals across BaseEntity.java and Visit.java returned no match), so whole-object comparison is unavailable.
approved_aspects: Placement matches system-design.md: the non-future-date rule and correction binding are assigned to VisitController and are tested through MockMvc at the web layer, the sanctioned mock. Pet.getVisit is a domain seam and has its own unit test in PetTests (found by identity, unknown id returns null), so no rule was covered only through the framework.
`./gradlew test` passes (BUILD SUCCESSFUL, jacocoTestReport ran).

coverage-map --feature REQ-VIS-003: 5 of 5 declared tests present, and every Done-when bullet has a test whose name states it. Bullet 3 (visit count unchanged) is theVisitEditShouldNotAddAVisitToThePet. Edge case 3 (unknown or other pet's visit) is the parameterized refusal test. Edge case 4 (past-dated visit resubmitted unchanged) is the third row of refusedCorrections.

New tests use the `the{Subject}Should{Outcome}` school, four-phase layout without narration comments, and named constants (BOOKED_VISIT_ID, OTHER_PETS_VISIT_ID, CORRECTED_DATE, etc.). Domain construction sits behind createAnOwner/createAPet/createAVisit factories.
The Mockito interaction checks (`save(owner)` once, `never().save(any())` on refusal) assert the persistence contract, which is the write path through OwnerRepository, not a restated outcome.

author: change-grader
summary: add in-place correction of a booked visit

blast_radius.note: Two production files in the owner package (Pet.getVisit, VisitController), one module, no sensitive paths. The shared visit loader now serves booking too, but the booking branch (newVisitFor) is the old body moved unchanged. The docs edits narrow NG-5 as the owner asked.

semantic_surprise.note: Read the loader branch, the extracted date check (same condition as before), the id-disallow binder, owner binding=false, and the getVisit filter. No inverted guard or silent booking change. Rejected corrections are never persisted because open-in-view is false and save is not reached. There is one cosmetic quirk: the reused template shows the Add Visit label on the edit form, and on a validation failure its Previous Visits table repeats the rejected values in memory.

test_adequacy.note: The build passed. The MockMvc tests check real outcomes: the form is prefilled, the same visit instance is mutated, save is called with the owner, the visit count is unchanged, each refused field is named with no save, foreign and unknown visit ids are refused, and id and owner-field tampering is ignored. The remaining gap is that the repository is mocked, so the cascade merge that updates the visit row is assumed rather than exercised. Booking uses the same pattern.

reviewer_hedging.note: All four reviewers approved, and the security citations I checked resolve (application.properties:11, VisitController.java:55, system-design.md:82). Two caveats remain. The test-reviewer's first-round tested-as-spec finding was fixed only with tests (the fix delta touches only VisitControllerTests), and its re-approval says the tests were not mutation-checked. The doc-reviewer's approval leaves a worry open: the 2026-08-08 ADR body still says a booked visit is immutable.

scope_deviation.note: There were no design revisions, consultations or build retries. No edit link, no template change, and cancellation stays out. The fix round touched only the test file. Edge case 4 (a past visit can only be saved by moving its date into the future) follows the owner's instruction to validate like booking, and it is recorded as an open PRD question.

rationale: The code is tight: the booking path is unchanged, tampering guards are pinned by tests, and nothing is persisted on refusal. Scrutinize is driven by reviewer caveats. Read the stale immutable-visit sentence the doc-reviewer left in the 2026-08-08 ADR, and consciously accept edge case 4: past visits cannot be corrected without moving their date forward.
